subject: Re: ZenCommerce — session affinity, burst profile, and sizing clarifications
messages:
From: Sophie Chan <sophie@zencommerce.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
Cc: ZenCommerce Sales Ops <ops@zencommerce.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ZenCommerce sizing — traffic, sessions, and cache questions

Hi Elliot,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As we scoped out Redwood Dedicated for ZenCommerce's recommendation engine and chat assistant, procurement asked for a short pre-sales questionnaire so we can compare committed capacity options. We're hoping to get a first-pass sizing recommendation from you before our internal review on Friday.

High-level context:
- Primary workload: customer-facing conversational assistant (90%) + batch reranking for recommendations (10%).
- Average concurrent users today: 120 active chat sessions; expected Q4 peak (holiday) concurrency ~1,200 sustained, with 15–20 minute hourly microbursts to ~3,500 for 8–12 minutes.

Can you help confirm the specific data points you need? To speed things up, here are the fields we believe are relevant — please confirm or add:
- Average prompt token count per request
- Average response token count (and max response length allowed)
- Typical session duration and session re-use (how long KV cache must be retained)
- Percent of requests benefiting from prefix/KV cache hits
- Latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99 targets we should assume)
- Any per-session memory (KV) or per-token compute considerations we should surface

If you prefer, attach the worksheet and we'll fill it with telemetry later today.

Thanks —
Sophie Chan
Head of Product, ZenCommerce
Sophie.Chan@zencommerce.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-3691

---
Attachment: none (will send telemetry after internal sync)

From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Chan <sophie@zencommerce.com>
Cc: ZenCommerce Sales Ops <ops@zencommerce.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ZenCommerce sizing — traffic, sessions, and cache questions

Sophie —

Thanks for the context, this is perfect. I've attached a compact worksheet (zen-sizing-worksheet.xlsx) that captures the fields we typically need for an initial Dedicated sizing sketch. Quick notes before you fill it out:

- For "average prompt/response tokens" give us both mean and 95th percentile if available — response token variance matters a lot for occupancy.
- Session affinity: tell us how often a user resumes a session within N minutes (we use this to size KV cache retention and per-session memory). If you have a distribution (percent reused within 5/30/60 minutes) that helps.
- Burst description: please clarify whether bursts are global or concentrated by region/tenant. If a small subset of tenants produces the bursts, we can recommend tenant shaping and queueing instead of firm capacity commits.
- Reranking batch jobs: provide average batch size and concurrency for those offline/rerank jobs; they can often be scheduled on lower-priority GPU pools.

I'll loop in Laura and Vivek from the capacity team for a quick recommendation once we have the completed worksheet and the telemetry snippet. If you can get the sample telemetry link and one hour of p99 latency traces, we can run a micro-simulation this week.

Proposed next step: you fill the worksheet and upload the telemetry to the S3 link in your reply. We can then put together a 1–page ballpark: GPU mix + reserved slot estimate + canary ramp plan.

Best,
Elliot Price
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
elliot_price@redwood.com

---
Attachments: zen-sizing-worksheet.xlsx

From: Sophie Chan <sophie@zencommerce.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
Cc: ZenCommerce Sales Ops <ops@zencommerce.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ZenCommerce sizing — traffic, sessions, and cache questions

Elliot —

Attached is a 1-hour sample export and a short answers sheet (telemetry-snippet.json). Key values filled in below to make the worksheet easier:

- Avg prompt tokens: 95 (p95: 260)
- Avg response tokens: 720 (p95: 2,100). We currently cap responses at 3,000 tokens for long-form content.
- Typical session duration: median 78s, mean 150s (heavy tails from longer customer service sessions); session re-use within 20 minutes: 42%; within 60 minutes: 67%.
- Peak sustained concurrency today: 1,200 (Q4 planning target sustained), microburst hourly spikes to 3,500 for 8–12 mins, global distribution but ~65% traffic is US-east.
- KV cache per active session (estimated): 80–120 KB (serialized turn history + embeddings pointers).
- Percent of requests benefiting from prefix/KV cache hits: ~58% (mostly short follow-ups).
- Rerank jobs: average batch size 128, run on lower-priority fleet asynchronously (not in the critical path).
- Latency SLOs: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 420ms (we can be flexible on p99 if cost tradeoff is documented).

Telemetry is at: s3://zencommerce-samples/telemetry/20270522-sample.json (public link shared via the ops mailbox).

Let us know if you need additional traces (we can export 24h), otherwise please share the ballpark later today.

Cheers,
Sophie

Attachment: telemetry-snippet.json

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Chan <sophie@zencommerce.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ZenCommerce sizing — session affinity, burst profile, and sizing clarifications

Hi Sophie / Elliot —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the telemetry link. We pulled the 1-hour sample and ran a short steady-state estimate and a burst sanity check. High-level ballpark (will refine with 24h traces):

- Recommended committed mix (ballpark): 30–40 H100 80GB nodes + 10–20 A100 80GB nodes, mapped to low-latency tier and batch tier respectively. This gives headroom for your Q4 sustained target and short microbursts when combined with autoscaling/burst credits.
- Prefix/KV cache sizing: cache retention window of 60 minutes for active session affinity. With 67% reuse and 100KB per-session average, plan for ~120 GB hot KV cache per 1,000 concurrent sessions.
- Batching & throughput: configure continuous micro-batching for short requests (p95 response under 220ms) and reserve a separate low-priority pool for reranks.
- Canary & rollout: recommend 5% canary ramp for 48 hours (validate p99 under load) then 25% for 24 hours before full switch. Include automatic fallback policy to the hosted model for degraded tail latency.

Action items:
- Sophie: if you can share 24 hours of p99 traces (tail latency across regions) we will run a more robust sim.
- Elliot: please prepare a short initial-sizing-proposal.pdf with the commit ranges, expected costs (monthly), and suggested SLA tiers.
- Vivek: please review the KV cache math and GPU mix and flag any constraints for private deployments (HSM/KMS throughput, region availability).

We'll aim to have the 1-page proposal by EOD PDT.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Capacity & Pricing — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: initial-sizing-proposal.pdf
